claim: The Drosophila larva transmission electron microscopy reconstruction is of a whole central nervous system.
source: Here, we use the transmission electron microscopy reconstruction of a whole central nervous system in the Drosophila larva to elucidate the sensory pathways and the interneurons that provide synaptic input to the neurosecretory cells projecting to the endocrine organs.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states that the EM reconstruction is of a whole CNS in the Drosophila larva.

claim: A new carbon dioxide-responsive network acts on neurosecretory cells expressing corazonin (Crz) and diuretic hormone 44 (Dh44) neuropeptides.
source: Predicted by network modeling, we also identify a new carbon dioxide-responsive network that acts on a specific set of neurosecretory cells and that includes those expressing corazonin (Crz) and diuretic hormone 44 (Dh44) neuropeptides.
evidence: The abstract states that network modeling predicted and the study identified a new CO2-responsive network targeting Crz and Dh44 neurons.

claim: The neuronal network architecture enables combinatorial action based on sensory and interneuronal pathways that converge onto distinct combinations of neuroendocrine outputs.
source: Our analysis reveals a neuronal network architecture for combinatorial action based on sensory and interneuronal pathways that converge onto distinct combinations of neuroendocrine outputs.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the network architecture as enabling combinatorial action through convergence of pathways.

claim: The pars intercerebralis (PI) and pars lateralis (PL) regions of the larval brain are considered analogous to the vertebrate hypothalamus.
source: The pars intercerebralis (PI) and pars lateralis (PL) regions of the larval brain are considered to be analogous to the vertebrate hypothalamus.
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this anatomical analogy.

claim: The ring gland (corpora cardiaca, corpus allatum, and prothoracic gland) exerts functions physiologically similar to the vertebrate pituitary gland.
source: The three known endocrine glands (collectively known as the ring gland) – the corpora cardiaca (CC), the corpus allatum (CA), and the prothoracic gland (PG) – exert functions that are physiologically similar to the vertebrate pituitary gland (de Velasco et al., 2007; Hartenstein, 2006; Scharrer and Scharrer, 1944).
evidence: The introduction explicitly states this functional analogy with citations to support the claim.

claim: All neurosecretory cell clusters that project to the ring gland were identified and compared to expression patterns of known peptide-Gal4 driver lines.
source: All neurosecretory cell clusters found previously by light microscopy analysis (Siegmund and Korge, 2001) were identified and compared to expression patterns of known peptide-Gal4 driver lines.
evidence: The results section states that all RPN clusters were identified and compared to Gal4 lines.

claim: 56 neurons innervate the ring gland.
source: Total number of neurons per RPN cluster: DMS = 4, IPCs = 14, DH44 = 6, CRZ = 6, ITP = 8, CA-LP = 6, PTTH = 4, HugRG = 4, CAPA = 2, EH = 2.
evidence: Figure 2B caption lists the total number of neurons per cluster, which sum to 56.

claim: Dense core vesicle (DCV) fusion sites were identified by contacts of DCVs with the membrane with apparent liberation of small dense particles.
source: The specific peptidergic output region of all cells was identified by contacts of DCVs with the membrane with the apparent liberation of small dense particles, as exemplified for the corazonin neurons (CRZ) (Figure 2C).
evidence: The results section describes the method for identifying DCV fusion sites with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: The outputs of all 10 peptidergic RPN groups are restricted mainly to the CC and AO.
source: The outputs of all 10 peptidergic RPN groups are restricted mainly to the CC and AO.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding about peptidergic outputs.

claim: PTTH neurons project almost exclusively to the PG.
source: PTTH and CA-LP project almost exclusively to the PG and CA, respectively (Figure 2D).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: CA-LP neurons project almost exclusively to the CA.
source: PTTH and CA-LP project almost exclusively to the PG and CA, respectively (Figure 2D).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 2D.

claim: Corazonin neurons (CRZ) showed the broadest output pattern, targeting all ring gland tissues.
source: Neurons producing the stress-related peptide Crz (Kubrak et al., 2016) showed the broadest output pattern, targeting all tissues (Figure 2C and D).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to figures and a citation.

claim: The CC cells are the main target of CRZ neurons.
source: Using Crz and corazonin receptor (CrzR)-expressing cells as an example, we could confirm by trans-Tango system (Inagaki et al., 2012) that the CC cells are the main target of CRZ (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The results section states this was confirmed using the trans-Tango system with citation.

claim: 30 downstream partners of RPNs were identified, all exclusively targeted by the two eclosion hormone neurons (EH).
source: We identified 30 downstream partners that, unexpectedly, were exclusively targeted by the two eclosion hormone neurons (EH), one on each side of the ventromedial protocerebrum (Figure 2E).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: EH neurons synaptically target all other RPNs except CA-LP and PTTH.
source: Notably, these include all the other RPNs with the exception of CA-LP and PTTH, which regulate the activity of two major growth/maturation hormones, namely juvenile hormone and ecdysone (Figure 2F).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 2F.

claim: 209 upstream partners of the RPNs were identified.
source: We identified 209 upstream partners of the RPNs, whose synaptic sites are distributed in the anterior thoracic and SEZ region and up along the protocerebrum in a sprinkler-like fashion (Figure 3A).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this number with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: RPNs in the PI (IPCs, DMS, DH44) have significant amounts of monosynaptic connections with sensory neurons.
source: Unlike the RPNs in the PI (IPCs, DMS, DH44), which have significant amounts of monosynaptic connections with sensory neurons (Miroschnikow et al., 2018; Schlegel et al., 2016), the RPNs of the PL (CRZ, PTTH, CA-LP, and ITP) have no direct sensory input.
evidence: The results section states this with citations to previous work.

claim: RPNs of the PL (CRZ, PTTH, CA-LP, and ITP) have no direct sensory input.
source: Unlike the RPNs in the PI (IPCs, DMS, DH44), which have significant amounts of monosynaptic connections with sensory neurons (Miroschnikow et al., 2018; Schlegel et al., 2016), the RPNs of the PL (CRZ, PTTH, CA-LP, and ITP) have no direct sensory input.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding with citations.

claim: EH, CAPA, and HugRG RPNs have only small amounts of direct sensory contacts.
source: Similarly, EH, CAPA, and HugRG (hugin neurons innervating ring gland) RPNs have only small amounts of direct sensory contacts (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Slightly more than half of all upstream neurons of RPNs integrate sensory information (n = 110).
source: We first divided the upstream interneurons into two groups: interneurons receiving direct sensory input and those that do not (threshold at two synapses); slightly more than half of all upstream neurons integrate sensory information, n = 110 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The results section explicitly states this number with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: A subset of tracheal dendritic neurons (TD neurons) are responsive to CO2 levels.
source: Here, we additionally characterize a subset of tracheal dendritic neurons (TD neurons) (Qian et al., 2018; Schlegel et al., 2016) as being responsive to CO2 levels (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The results section states this characterization with citations and reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: In vivo experiments confirmed the predictions for DH44 and CRZ RPNs, which were strongly activated by CO2.
source: Indeed, the in vivo experiments confirmed the predictions for DH44 and CRZ RPNs, which were strongly activated by CO2 (Figure 4).
evidence: The results section states that experiments confirmed the model predictions with reference to Figure 4.

claim: Weaker activation of DMS and IPCs by CO2 was observed, consistent with the predicted weak effects.
source: Weaker activation of DMS and IPCs was also observed, consistent with the predicted weak effects.
evidence: The results section states this observation and its consistency with predictions.

claim: CAPA neurons did not differ significantly from control groups but tended to show lower activity upon CO2 stimulation.
source: CAPA neurons did not differ significantly from control groups but tended to show a lower activity upon CO2 stimulation.
evidence: The results section states this observation about CAPA neurons.

claim: A core set of four thoracic interneurons (somata located in T1–T3 segments) integrate CO2 information from TD neurons and strongly connect to DH44 and CRZ.
source: The analysis of connectivity based on the EM volume enabled us to identify a new circuit in which CO2 level is detected by TD neurons, integrated by a core set of four thoracic interneurons (somata located in T1–T3 segments), which in turn strongly connect to DH44 and CRZ (Figure 5A and B).
evidence: The results section explicitly describes this circuit with reference to figures.

claim: Each of the four thoracic interneurons have slightly different connectivity profiles in terms of their up- and downstream partners.
source: Each of the thoracic interneurons have slightly different connectivity profiles in terms of their up- and downstream partners (Figure 5C).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: For CRZ, the strongest upstream interneuron is Munin 2 (#10), which accounts for over 50% of total synaptic input to the CRZ neurons.
source: For CRZ, the strongest are in fact not the thoracic interneurons from the CO2 pathway: one hemilateral pair of interneurons (#10, Munin 2) accounts for over 50% of total synaptic input to the CRZ neurons.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this quantitative finding.

claim: Munin 2 interneurons receive sensory information exclusively from pharyngeal sensory neurons.
source: These interneurons receive sensory information exclusively from pharyngeal sensory neurons (Figure 5D, top hive plot).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: For DH44, the strongest upstream partners are the thoracic interneurons that respond to CO2.
source: For DH44, the strongest upstream partners are the same thoracic interneurons that respond to CO2 (Figure 5D, bottom hive plot).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 5D.

claim: Gustatory receptor 21a (Gr21a) is responsive to CO2.
source: Currently, one chemosensory receptor, gustatory receptor 21a (Gr21a), has been shown to be responsive to CO2 (Faucher et al., 2006).
evidence: The results section states this with a citation.

claim: Gr21a is expressed in the terminal organ but not in the TD neurons.
source: It is expressed in the terminal organ, which is located in the anterior part of the larvae, but not in the TD neurons (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: Connectivity analysis of the chemosensory projections of the terminal and ventral organs reveals only very weak connections to the DH44 or CRZ neurons.
source: Although we cannot determine the precise projections of the Gr21a-expressing neurons in the EM volume, a connectivity analysis of the chemosensory projections of the terminal and ventral organs (we cannot differentiate between projections originating from TO and VO in the EM volume) reveals only very weak connections to the DH44 or CRZ neurons, suggesting that CO2-responsive Gr21a terminal organ and TD neuronal pathways are largely independent (Figure 5—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The results section states this finding with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: IPCs receive inputs from the largest number of interneurons with direct sensory connections.
source: For instance, the IPCs receive inputs from the largest number of such interneurons, and from these, interneuron #11 (HuginPC, hugin neurons innervating protocerebrum) provides the largest input.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: HugRG neurons receive inputs from the least number of interneurons with direct sensory connections.
source: At the other extreme, HugRG neurons receive inputs from the least number of such interneurons; however, one of these, namely #17 (Dpilp7), provides 8% of total input that the HugRG neurons receive.
evidence: The results section explicitly states this finding.

claim: HugPC interneurons have their strongest inputs from the enteric sensory neurons and strongly target just the IPCs.
source: For example, both #11 (HugPC) and #12 (SiB) interneurons have their strongest inputs from the enteric sensory neurons; however, whereas HugPC interneurons strongly target just the IPCs (edge threshold of minimum five synapses), SiB interneurons target DMS, IPCs, and CRZ (Figure 6C).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: SiB interneurons have their strongest inputs from the enteric sensory neurons and target DMS, IPCs, and CRZ.
source: For example, both #11 (HugPC) and #12 (SiB) interneurons have their strongest inputs from the enteric sensory neurons; however, whereas HugPC interneurons strongly target just the IPCs (edge threshold of minimum five synapses), SiB interneurons target DMS, IPCs, and CRZ (Figure 6C).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to Figure 6C.

claim: Interneurons (#s 46–50) are highly specialized for CA-LP and PTTH and receive strong sensory inputs from the olfactory system.
source: There are also intriguing unique groups, for example, the interneurons (#s 46–50), which are highly specialized for CA-LP and PTTH (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2); these receive strong sensory inputs from the olfactory system (for a comprehensive connectivity map, see Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The results section states this with references to figures.

claim: In adult Drosophila, the release of juvenile hormone from the CA potentiates sensitivity of a pheromone sensing olfactory receptor OR47b to maximize courtship success of male flies.
source: In adult Drosophila, it was shown that the release of juvenile hormone from the CA potentiates sensitivity of a pheromone sensing olfactory receptor OR47b (Lin et al., 2016) to maximize courtship success of male flies.
evidence: The results section states this with a citation.

claim: Several previously appetitive and aversive assigned olfactory receptor neurons are connected via multiglomerular projection neurons to the CA-LP and PTTH neurons in larvae.
source: In larvae, we found several previously appetitive and aversive assigned olfactory receptor neurons (Kreher et al., 2008) being connected via multiglomerular projection neurons to the CA-LP and PTTH neurons.
evidence: The results section states this finding with a citation.

claim: Parallel paths exist from sensory to the mushroom body and lateral horn, through additional layers of interneurons (including mushroom body output neurons), and onto the CA-LP and PTTH neuroendocrine targets.
source: We also reveal parallel paths from sensory to the mushroom body and lateral horn, through additional layers of interneurons (which include mushroom body output neurons), and onto the CA-LP and PTTH neuroendocrine targets (Figure 6—figure supplement 3).
evidence: The results section states this with reference to a supplementary figure.

claim: A general feature of the ring gland projection neurons (RPNs) is the absence of synaptic outputs within the CNS, with the exception of EH-producing neurons.
source: A general feature of the ring gland projection neurons (RPNs) is the absence of synaptic outputs within the CNS. The exception are the EH-producing neurons, which have synaptic outputs in the protocerebrum, SEZ, and VNC.
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this general feature and its exception.

claim: The unique feature of EH neurons having synaptic outputs might be due to their function in coordinating movements during larval cuticle shedding.
source: This unique feature of EH neurons might be due to their function in coordinating movements during larval cuticle shedding (Baker et al., 1999; Krüger et al., 2015).
evidence: The discussion section states this speculation with citations.

claim: RPNs of the PL are connected with the sensory organs exclusively via polysynaptic paths, in contrast to the numerous monosynaptic connections found for RPNs of the PI.
source: Another feature is that the RPNs of the PL are connected with the sensory organs exclusively via polysynaptic paths, which is in contrast to the numerous monosynaptic connections found for RPNs of the PI (Miroschnikow et al., 2018; Schlegel et al., 2016).
evidence: The discussion section states this finding with citations.

claim: Peptides known for their roles in metabolic and stress regulation receive large amounts of their inputs from interneurons with direct contacts to the sensory system.
source: It is also noteworthy that peptides known for their roles in metabolic and stress regulation in general receive large amounts of their inputs from interneurons with direct contacts to the sensory system, that is, these paths are short, with only a single hop between the interneurons and sensory neurons.
evidence: The discussion section states this observation.

claim: The short sensory-to-neuroendocrine paths for metabolic and stress regulation peptides might be due to the need for rapid action compared to those involved in gradual, long-term and irreversible events such as larval growth and maturation.
source: This might be due to the need for rapid action compared to those (e.g., PTTH and CA-LP neurons) involved in gradual, long-term and irreversible events such as larval growth and maturation.
evidence: The discussion section speculates on the reason for this observation.

claim: High levels of CO2 are associated with stress in humans.
source: This might be due to the stress associated with high levels of CO2, which is observed in humans as well (Permentier et al., 2017).
evidence: The discussion section states this with a citation.

claim: Dh44 is a homolog of vertebrate CRH, which is released in the hypothalamus in response to external and internal stressors like hypoxia or hypoglycemia.
source: Dh44 is a homolog of vertebrate CRH, which is released in the hypothalamus in response to external and internal stressors like hypoxia or hypoglycemia (Flanagan et al., 2003).
evidence: The discussion section states this with a citation.

claim: A role for Dh44 in glucose and amino acid sensing has been reported.
source: A role for Dh44 in glucose and amino acid sensing has been reported (Dus et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2018), but its role in CO2-dependent response was not previously known.
evidence: The discussion section states this with citations.

claim: The role of Dh44 in CO2-dependent response was not previously known.
source: A role for Dh44 in glucose and amino acid sensing has been reported (Dus et al., 2015; Yang et al., 2018), but its role in CO2-dependent response was not previously known.
evidence: The discussion section states this.

claim: Crz is a homolog to GnRH.
source: CO2 activation of Crz, a homolog to GnRH, adds to the repertoire of stress sensors ascribed to these neurons that include their roles in glucose and fructose sensing (Dus et al., 2015; Kubrak et al., 2016; Miyamoto and Amrein, 2014; Oh et al., 2019; Veenstra, 2009).
evidence: The discussion section states this with citations.

claim: CRZ neurons have roles in glucose and fructose sensing.
source: CO2 activation of Crz, a homolog to GnRH, adds to the repertoire of stress sensors ascribed to these neurons that include their roles in glucose and fructose sensing (Dus et al., 2015; Kubrak et al., 2016; Miyamoto and Amrein, 2014; Oh et al., 2019; Veenstra, 2009).
evidence: The discussion section states this with citations.

claim: The CO2 sensory pathway that originates in the trachea appears to be largely distinct from the CO2 sensing pathway that originates in the terminal organ.
source: The connectome analysis further indicates that CRZ and DH44 neurons have the strongest synaptic connections with the sensory system (i.e., greatest number of paths that are connected monosynaptically or via single interneurons), suggesting a critical role of these neurosecretory cells in rapid sensory integration.
evidence: The discussion section states this inference based on the connectome analysis.

claim: CRZ and DH44 neurons have the strongest synaptic connections with the sensory system, suggesting a critical role of these neurosecretory cells in rapid sensory integration.
source: The connectome analysis further indicates that CRZ and DH44 neurons have the strongest synaptic connections with the sensory system (i.e., greatest number of paths that are connected monosynaptically or via single interneurons), suggesting a critical role of these neurosecretory cells in rapid sensory integration.
evidence: The discussion section states this inference.

claim: At the core of the neuroendocrine network is a parallel set of interneurons that target distinct combinations of neuroendocrine outputs.
source: At the core of the neuroendocrine network is a parallel set of interneurons that target distinct combinations of neuroendocrine outputs (e.g., the RPNs, each expressing certain neuropeptides).
evidence: The discussion section explicitly describes this network architecture.

claim: Each of the interneurons in the neuroendocrine network receive sensory inputs from distinct sets of sensory neurons.
source: Each of the interneurons in turn receive sensory inputs from distinct sets of sensory neurons (e.g., CO2 sensitive in trachea or different type and modality within the pharyngeal region).
evidence: The discussion section states this.

claim: Multiglomerular projection neurons integrate olfactory as well as gustatory information.
source: Multiglomerular projection neurons integrate olfactory as well as gustatory information, and as one proceeds deeper into the neuronal circuitry, interneurons that have originally been classified as interneurons without sensory input can be connected by additional hops to sensory neurons (such as through mushroom body and lateral horn in the protocerebrum).
evidence: The discussion section states this.

claim: The different converging paths in the neuroendocrine network can be seen to represent distinct types of sensory information, including a stored form from the mushroom body.
source: The different converging paths can be seen to represent distinct types of sensory information, including a stored form from the mushroom body (Eichler et al., 2017; Eschbach and Zlatic, 2020; Miroschnikow et al., 2020), where a positive or negative valence has been attached to an existing sensory cue.
evidence: The discussion section states this with citations.

claim: The network architecture would enable variability and flexibility in the combination and concentrations of neuropeptides that become released in response to multisensory inputs.
source: Such architecture would enable variability and flexibility in the combination and concentrations of neuropeptides that become released in response to the flood of multisensory inputs that act on all parts of the neuroendocrine network.
evidence: The discussion section states this inference about the functional implications of the architecture.

claim: Cross-regulatory interactions at the receptor level would determine the final neuropeptide/hormone composition that is released within the CNS or into the circulation.
source: Subsequently cross-regulatory interactions at the receptor level would then determine the final neuropeptide/hormone composition that is released within the CNS or into the circulation.
evidence: The discussion section states this inference.

claim: The neuroendocrine connectome of the Drosophila larva represents the first complete synaptic map of sensory to endocrine pathways in a neuroendocrine system of this complexity.
source: As a concluding remark, the neuroendocrine connectome of the Drosophila larva presented here (i.e., the 'ring gland connectome') represents the first complete synaptic map of sensory to endocrine pathways in a neuroendocrine system of this complexity and adds another level of insight on the known humoral functions of the released neuropeptides and hormones.
evidence: The discussion section explicitly states this claim.

claim: The ssTEM volume was generated from a 6-hr-old first instar larva.
source: Neuron reconstruction was done on an ssTEM volume of a 6-hr-old first instar larva (Ohyama et al., 2015).
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this with a citation.

claim: All neurons projecting to the ring gland were reconstructed to completion (tracing 100% and at least 95% reviewed).
source: We reconstructed all neurons to completion (tracing 100% and at least 95% reviewed).
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this.

claim: All synaptic up- and downstream partners of the RPNs were reconstructed to completion with a synaptic threshold to each of the RPNs of three synapses.
source: All synaptic up- and downstream partners of the RPNs were reconstructed to completion with a synaptic threshold to each of the RPNs of three synapses.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this.

claim: All 26 TD neurons were reconstructed for this study.
source: A subset of 12 TD neurons were already described (Schlegel et al., 2016). We reconstructed for this study all 26 TD neurons.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this with a citation.

claim: The feed forward network (FFN) was implemented in Python as a simple artificial neural network without backpropagation.
source: The FFN was implemented in Python as a simple artificial neural network without backpropagation.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this.

claim: Neurons in the FFN were implemented as rectified linear units using a ReLu activation function that starts responding at 5% and reaches saturation at 50% of their synaptic inputs being active.
source: Neurons were implemented as rectified linear units using a ReLu activation function that starts responding at 5% and reaches saturation at 50% of their synaptic inputs being active
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this.

claim: The values for the ReLu activation function were chosen to maximize the response range of the network.
source: These values were chosen to maximize the response range of the network.
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this.

claim: The code for the FFN and the generation of the figures can be found at https://github.com/Pankratz-Lab/FFN_Hueckesfeld-et-al.-2020.
source: The code for the FFN and the generation of the figures can be found at https://github.com/Pankratz-Lab/FFN_Hueckesfeld-et-al.-2020 (Schoofs and Schlegel, 2020; copy archived at swh:1:rev:494220124eb79f5ed0b5eebe585b796e18729b47).
evidence: The Materials and methods section states this with a citation.
